page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 124 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.88 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4d-standard-32 demonstrates top-tier single-core capabilities, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3. Multi-core performance is also strong, with Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores landing in the top tier and top 25% respectively. Cryptographic and vector execution are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels, while static web serving throughput and small-model LLM text generation show strong to top-tier efficiency.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-32 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring high single-thread performance and modern instruction sets without the added cost of bundled GPUs or local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times. This profile is appropriate for software compilation, web serving, image and text processing, and moderate-scale machine learning inference tasks.
